installed.caption: Calvin's observation at Emerald Pass, Kyle, on 2025-09-24. Follow each flower down to its folded green spathe. The two large blue petals occur in both dayflower genera; use the spathe and filament hairs to separate them.

installed.role: Flower macro — smooth filaments and lobed yellow staminodes
installed.caption: Look at the smooth, curved filaments below the petals and the small lobed yellow staminodes above them. Commelina erecta has three fertile stamens plus three staminodes. The dense purple-and-yellow filament tufts of Tinantia are absent. Do not count the pistil as a stamen.
installed.creator: Nathan Taylor

verification.limits: No scale; this photograph is used only for the visible structures identified in the caption.

installed.role: Joey macro — purple-and-yellow beards on stamen filaments
installed.caption: The purple-and-yellow tufts are hairs on the filaments, not extra petals. Tinantia has six fertile stamens; five filaments are bearded, with the lower central filament smooth. Compare this image directly with Commelina erecta's smooth filament macro. The little white lower petal is also visible.
installed.creator: Joey Santore

verification.limits: No scale; this photograph is used only for the visible structures identified in the caption.

installed.role: Side view — exposed cyme above an open leaflike bract
installed.caption: Trace the stalk from the open flower past the buds to the broad green bract below the cluster. The bract spreads outward instead of enclosing the entire cluster in a fused Commelina-style pocket. The boatlike green coverings immediately around individual buds are sepals; do not confuse those with a spathe.
installed.creator: River Wilder
